text:
Situation: Ketamine hydrochloride is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 39 vials of the 50 mg/mL, 10 mL presentation at 7.2 vials per day (5.4 days on hand). Corvale General holds 126 vials of the same presentation at 7.7 vials per day (16.4 days on hand). The best option by rule is to transfer 18 vials of 50 mg/mL, 10 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East, leaving Corvale General with 14 days and bringing Corvale East to 8 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA's history shows an earlier shortage first posted on 2018-02-16, since resolved. FDA inspection 976095 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 618 days before the 2018-02-16 posting. A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira, Inc. on 2017-02-14, 367 days before the posting. FDA inspection 1031233 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2017-10-27 and was classified VAI, 112 days before the posting.

Our position: No national shortage exists today. Local inventory at Corvale East is below target for the 50 mg/mL, 10 mL vial. Corvale General has sufficient stock to support a transfer while maintaining a two-week supply.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 18 vials of ketamine hydrochloride 50 mg/mL, 10 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval: Pharmacy Director; controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V) required.
2. Transfer 15 vials of ketamine hydrochloride 100 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside. Approval: Pharmacy Director; controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V) required.
3. Transfer 81 vials of ketamine hydrochloride 100 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval: Pharmacy Director; controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V) required.
4. Purchase additional supply from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC. Approval: Buyer.
5. Purchase additional supply from Par Health USA, LLC. Approval: Buyer.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or formulary substitutions; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
